title: Pluggable search, rules and visitors
idea: An extensible file system takes new filters, tree operations and write rules as new classes; after a one-time `accept` hook, nodes and facade stay untouched.
points: A `Criteria` is a strategy; `and` and `negate` combine small filters.
A `NodeVisitor` adds an operation, such as bytes per extension, as one class.
`WriteRule` checks run as a chain before every create; any rule can refuse.
A registry maps config names to rule factories; unknown names fail at startup.

code.title: Criteria, visitor, rule chain
code.caption: `Volume` is a trimmed `FileSystem` facade. A config string picks three write rules; filters combine; a visitor adds a report without touching the nodes.

walk.text: Config names three rules and gives each one its setting.
Four files pass the rules; three more are each refused by a different rule.
Filters combine with `and` and `negate`; `find` never changes.
Each filter is a lambda; the default methods build bigger ones.
The visitor walks the tree and sums bytes per extension.
The registry turns config names into rules, refusing unknown names at once.
Every create runs the whole chain first, then adds the file.

pitfalls: Do not add `if (ext.equals(...))` branches to `create`; add a `WriteRule`.
Validate configuration when the volume is built, not on the first write.
Use a visitor only when node kinds are stable; each new kind edits every visitor.

quiz.q: Which `refused` message does the `big.log` create print?
quiz.why: The volume already holds 5700 bytes. Adding 900 passes the name rules but goes over the 6000-byte quota, so the last rule in the chain refuses it.

takeaway: New behaviour arrives as a class and a registry entry, not an edit.
